q: ____ is the movement of dissolved substances through a plant.
e: Translocation refers specifically to the transport of organic solutes in the phloem.

q: In general, water and dissolved salts from the soil travel upwards through the vessels of the xylem and food synthesized in the leaves passes downwards or upwards in the ____ of the phloem.
e: Sieve tubes are the conducting channels for translocation in the phloem.
Carbohydrates are the primary organic products of photosynthesis.

q: These carbohydrates are transported out of the leaf in the form of ____ to the stem.
e: Sucrose is the main transport sugar used in phloem translocation.

q: Once in the stem it may travel upwards to actively growing regions or maturing fruits and seeds or downwards to the roots and underground ____ organs.
e: Phloem transports sugars to storage organs like roots and tubers.

q: Both upward and downward movement may take place at the ____ time in the phloem.
e: Phloem can transport materials in multiple directions simultaneously depending on source and sink.

q: The phloem tissue is a ____ tissue.
e: Phloem is a complex tissue composed of multiple different cell types.

q: The consisting components are sieve tube, ____ cell, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibre.
e: Companion cells are essential components of the phloem tissue.

q: They are ____ cells except phloem fibre.
e: Most phloem components are living cells, unlike the dead xylem vessels.

q: They are so called because of the presence of perforations in the cell septate walls known as ____.
e: Sieve plates allow the flow of sap between adjacent sieve tube elements.

q: Sieve cells can manage translocation without nuclei because they are kept alive by the nucleated ____ cells that always situated adjacent to sieve cells.
e: Companion cells provide the metabolic support and energy required by sieve cells.

q: Moreover, phloem tissue is strengthened by ____ cells besides the sieve and companion cells.
e: Phloem fibres provide mechanical strength and support to the tissue.
